story_title: The Mystery of the Misty Jar
story_description: Eight classmates investigate droplets on a cold jar and connect condensation to clouds and rain.
learning_objectives: Observe and explain condensation on a cold surface
Connect condensation to how clouds and rain form

panels.description: Teacher places a clear glass jar with ice on a tray. The eight students gather around, curious.
panels.narration: A strange science mystery appears in Class 5B.

dialogue.speaker: Teacher
dialogue.text: Watch this cold jar closely today.

dialogue.speaker: Maya Rivers
dialogue.text: It already looks frosty and spooky!

panels.setting: Same classroom table, a few minutes later
panels.description: Tiny droplets appear on the outside of the jar. Leo leans in; Priya scribbles notes.

dialogue.speaker: Leo Martinez
dialogue.text: Hey, water drops are growing on the glass!

dialogue.speaker: Priya Shah
dialogue.text: But nobody poured water there. Weird.

panels.description: Finn sketches the jar, Sophie points at the window where clouds are visible, and Noah watches thoughtfully.
panels.narration: The mystery of the jar deepens.

dialogue.speaker: Sophie Miller
dialogue.text: It's like tiny clouds on the glass.

dialogue.speaker: Noah Chen
dialogue.text: Where did this water really come from?

panels.description: Amara gently touches a droplet while Eli holds a dry paper towel near the jar.

dialogue.speaker: Amara Johnson
dialogue.text: The outside felt dry before, right?

dialogue.speaker: Eli Williams
dialogue.text: Yeah, this towel beside it is still dry.

panels.setting: Same table, Teacher writes words on the board
panels.description: The board reads 'water vapor,' 'cooling,' and 'condense.' Students glance between the jar and board.

dialogue.speaker: Teacher
dialogue.text: Clue one: air has invisible water vapor.

dialogue.speaker: Priya Shah
dialogue.text: So air is hiding water around us?

panels.setting: Close-up of the jar and board diagram
panels.description: Teacher sketches vapor arrows hitting the cold jar and turning into droplets. Maya raises a hand.
panels.narration: Cooling changes invisible vapor into tiny liquid drops.

dialogue.speaker: Teacher
dialogue.text: Clue two: cold things make vapor cool and condense.

dialogue.speaker: Maya Rivers
dialogue.text: So water in the air sticks as drops?

panels.setting: Classroom window showing bright sky and clouds
panels.description: Students gather at the window. Big puffy clouds float outside while Finn holds his jar sketch beside them.

dialogue.speaker: Finn Murphy
dialogue.text: These clouds look like giant versions of the jar.

dialogue.speaker: Sophie Miller
dialogue.text: Do clouds also start as water vapor?

panels.setting: Window area with a view of the sky and sun
panels.description: Noah imagines arrows rising from a lake outside while Amara traces the path upward through the air.

dialogue.speaker: Noah Chen
dialogue.text: Sun heats lakes. Water turns to vapor, right?

dialogue.speaker: Amara Johnson
dialogue.text: Then the warm vapor rises into cooler sky air.

panels.setting: Front of classroom, board showing sky layers
panels.description: Teacher draws rising vapor arrows, then small droplets bunching into a cloud shape.
panels.narration: The class connects the jar to the whole sky.

dialogue.speaker: Teacher
dialogue.text: Higher air is cooler. Vapor there condenses too.

dialogue.speaker: Leo Martinez
dialogue.text: So clouds are collections of tiny droplets!

panels.setting: Same board, now adding falling raindrop arrows
panels.description: Eli mimes big raindrops falling while Sophie draws raindrop shapes in her notebook.

dialogue.speaker: Eli Williams
dialogue.text: What if droplets bump, join, and get heavy?

dialogue.speaker: Sophie Miller
dialogue.text: Then gravity pulls them down as rain.

panels.description: Students sit in a circle, passing the cold jar around carefully while summarizing.

dialogue.speaker: Priya Shah
dialogue.text: Jar mystery: cooling air made vapor condense to drops.

dialogue.speaker: Finn Murphy
dialogue.text: Clouds form the same way, but up in the sky.

panels.setting: Front of classroom, everyone facing the reader
panels.description: All eight students and Teacher stand beside a board diagram showing jar, cloud, and rain arrows.
panels.narration: The whole class explains the water cycle step.

dialogue.speaker: Maya Rivers
dialogue.text: Water vapor rises and cools in the sky.

dialogue.speaker: Noah Chen
dialogue.text: It condenses into clouds, then falls back as rain.
